title: Sort Linked List by Frequency
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list of integers, sort its nodes in **decreasing order of value frequency** (values that occur more frequently appear earlier in the list).

If two distinct values have the **same frequency**, place the **smaller numeric value** first. Return the head of the sorted linked list.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Count the frequency of every node value in one pass using a hash map.
Sort the nodes using the composite comparator `(-freq[node.val], node.val)` and relink their `next` pointers (ending with `tail.next = null`).

examples.explanation: 2 and 3 both occur twice (2 < 3), while 1, 4, and 8 occur once each (1 < 4 < 8), producing [2, 2, 3, 3, 1, 4, 8].
Values -1 occurs three times and 2 occurs twice, producing [-1, -1, -1, 2, 2].
All values occur once, so tie-breaking sorts them in ascending order [-5, 0, 3, 9].
